SEC Obtains Final Judgment Against Former Crypto Lending Executive

Published 2026-10-06 19:30 UTC

The Securities and Exchange Commission today announced that it obtained a final judgment against a former executive of a crypto lending platform for his role in a scheme that misled investors about the platform's risks and financial condition.

The SEC's complaint, filed last year, alleged that the former executive, who served as chief revenue officer, made false statements to investors about the safety of the platform's lending program. He allegedly told investors that the platform only made overcollateralized loans to institutional borrowers, when in fact a large share of loans were unsecured or made to affiliated entities.

The final judgment orders the former executive to pay disgorgement of $3.2 million, prejudgment interest of $410,000, and a civil penalty of $1.5 million. It also permanently bars him from serving as an officer or director of a public company and enjoins him from violating the antifraud provisions of the federal securities laws.

The former executive consented to the entry of the final judgment without admitting or denying the allegations in the complaint. The court entered the judgment in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York.

The SEC's litigation against other defendants in the case is ongoing. The platform halted withdrawals two years ago and later filed for bankruptcy, leaving thousands of retail investors unable to access their assets.

The SEC encourages investors to be cautious about high-yield crypto products and to review the risks carefully before investing. Information on crypto asset risks is available on the SEC's investor education website.

The SEC's investigation was conducted by the Division of Enforcement's Crypto Assets and Cyber Unit. The agency thanked the court-appointed bankruptcy examiner for assistance with the case. Investors with information about potential violations of the securities laws involving crypto asset platforms can submit tips through the SEC's online portal.
